lessons: Use second-person immersive roleplay in hooks ('तुम एक...') to maximize early retention (achieved highest 10% retention at 1.0488).
Avoid dumping heavy technical terms or precise numerical forces (e.g., '34,500 Newton') early, as it caused the largest single drop in the dataset (-23% at 23% mark).
Anchor science concepts around clear visual comparisons (e.g., T. rex vs car speed) to sustain strong mid-video retention (49.3% kept at 50%).
Ensure the post-hook transition (11-12% mark) is seamless, as every video suffered a significant drop-off (11% to 19%) right after the hook.
worst_moment_types: Dense numerical or technical estimation explanations early in the video (e.g., jaw muscle Newton calculations).
Abstract physics law drops without immediate narrative momentum (e.g., referencing Newton's second law).
Transitions immediately following the main hook line at the 11-12% mark.
best_hook_types: Second-person immersive scenarios ('सोचो, तुम एक baby tyrannosaur हो...').
High-stakes comparison questions ('क्या T. rex तुम्हारी Car से तेज़ दौड़ सकता था?').
